acceptanceCriteria: When a customer purchases a return trip ticket with a promo code applied, the Mozio email confirmation displays the promo code discount amount for BOTH the outbound trip and the return trip.

When the email confirmation is rendered for a return trip order, the promo code discount line item appears under the return trip section with the correct discount amount matching the value applied to the outbound trip section.

When a customer purchases a one-way trip ticket with a promo code applied, the Mozio email confirmation continues to display the promo code discount amount correctly for the single trip, with no regression from the current behavior.

When a return trip order contains multiple line items (e.g., different fare types such as senior), the promo code discount amount is displayed for each line item's return portion, not just the first return line item.

When a promo code discount amount is zero or the promo code does not apply to the return portion, the email confirmation does not display a promo discount line for the return trip, avoiding showing a misleading zero-value or null entry.

When the order payload contains a return trip with dateFrom and dateTo fields spanning different dates, the promo code discount amount is displayed for the return trip regardless of the date range difference between outbound and return segments.

When the email confirmation template is generated, the system logs include an entry confirming the promo code discount amount was calculated and included for both outbound and return trip segments, enabling verification via application logs.

before.title: [Mozio] - The Promo code amount is NOT displayed as expected for Return trip tickets in the Mozio email confirmation

acceptanceCriteria: When a return trip dispatch is constructed, the report.price.discount field is populated with the promo code discount amount, mirroring how it is populated for the outbound dispatch.

When mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch processes a return-trip dispatch that contains report.price.discount, the discount name and amount are preserved in the SanitizedMozioDispatch output (no data loss during sanitization).
When a one-way trip ticket with a promo code is processed, the existing discount display behavior in the Mozio email confirmation is unchanged (no regression).

When a return trip order contains multiple line items (e.g., different fare types), each return line item's dispatch includes the applicable promo code discount amount, not just the first return line item.

When the promo code discount amount is zero or undefined for the return portion, the discount field is omitted (not set to a zero-value or null entry) in the return dispatch's report.price, preventing a misleading display in the email.
after.description: The promo code discount amount is not displayed for return trip tickets in the Mozio email confirmation. The root cause is that when return-trip dispatches are assembled (in the reservation/submit mapping layer), the report.price.discount is not propagated from the order's promo code data into the return dispatch, unlike the outbound dispatch which receives it correctly. The sanitization mapper (mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch) passes discount through faithfully, so the fix must ensure the discount is present in the return dispatch payload before sanitization.
after.title: [Mozio] - Promo code discount amount missing from return trip dispatch in Mozio email confirmation

notes: The bug is that promo code discount amount is missing from return-trip dispatches sent to Mozio. The data flow: reservation/submit mappers build MozioDispatch objects (including report.price.discount), then mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch sanitizes them before submission. The return-trip station-swap logic in create-reservations.mappers.ts already handles from/to swapping for return trips but does NOT propagate the discount into the return dispatch's report.price.discount. The sanitized mapper faithfully passes through whatever discount is present, so the root cause is upstream in how the return-trip dispatch is assembled.

acceptanceCriteria: When a return trip dispatch is constructed, the report.price.discount field contains the same promo code discount name and amount as the outbound dispatch's report.price.discount field.

When mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch processes a return-trip dispatch that contains report.price.discount, the discount name and amount are preserved in the SanitizedMozioDispatch output (no data loss during sanitization).

When a one-way trip ticket with a promo code is processed, the outbound dispatch's report.price.discount name and amount remain identical to their values before this change (no regression in one-way trip discount propagation).

When a return trip order contains multiple line items (e.g., different fare types), each return line item's dispatch includes the applicable promo code discount amount, not just the first return line item.

When the promo code discount amount is zero or undefined for the return portion, the discount field is omitted from the return dispatch's report.price (not set to a zero-value or null entry), consistent with how the outbound dispatch handles zero or undefined discounts.

When a return trip order has no promo code applied, the return dispatch's report.price does not contain a discount field, matching the behavior of the outbound dispatch for orders without promo codes.

When the promo code data for a return trip contains a discount name but the amount is missing or non-numeric, the entire discount field is omitted from the return dispatch's report.price (no partial discount objects with a name but no valid amount).

When a return trip dispatch is constructed, the discount name in report.price.discount matches the promo code display name, consistent with how the outbound dispatch populates the discount name (not just the amount is propagated).

notes: Refined AC1 to replace vague 'mirroring how it is populated' with a concrete observable: same discount name AND amount as outbound. Refined AC3 to specify exactly what 'unchanged' means (outbound dispatch discount name and amount remain identical to pre-fix values). Refined AC5 to add 'consistent with how the outbound dispatch handles zero or undefined discounts' so the return behavior is anchored to a reference. Added AC6: no-promo-code return trip edge case (omission of discount field when no promo exists on the order). Added AC7: malformed/partial discount data edge case — if amount is missing or non-numeric, omit the entire discount object rather than producing a partial entry. Added AC8: explicit coverage that the discount NAME (not just amount) must propagate to the return dispatch, since the original bug description mentions 'discount amount' but the discount object likely has both a name and amount field, and both are needed for email display. Flagged AC4's use of 'applicable' as vague — it is unclear whether the discount is prorated across line items, applied uniformly, or only applies to certain fare types.
